Villagers came out of their homes to confront the settlers, officials said. The ​subsequent shootout joined a growing series of clashes involving settlers in which dozens of Palestinians have been killed this ​year and hundreds wounded, according to figures from the U.N. and the Palestinian Authority. Abdel Azim Wadi, ⁠head of the village council in Qusra, southeast of Nablus, said settlers had torched a newly completed mosque in his ​village early on Sunday. He said they sprayed slogans in Hebrew on the walls, with messages including 'Jewish revenge' and the name of one ​of the Israelis killed near Tal. "The village has faced repeated attacks since 2011, and these attacks have increased since the war," he told Reuters by telephone. JEWISH SETTLEMENTS WIDELY CONSIDERED ILLEGAL Most countries and United Nations bodies consider Jewish settlements in the West Bank illegal, a position Israel rejects, ​while the Palestinians seek to establish an independent state in Gaza, the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Since Israel launched a war against Gaza's ​Palestinian Hamas rulers in October 2023, after Gaza militants killed more than 1,000 Israelis, settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank have ‌increased sharply. The ⁠Israeli military said troops sent to Qusra, which sits near several large Israeli settlements, had found graffiti and signs of arson and were searching for suspects. It said police officers would be sent to collect evidence. "The security forces strongly condemn incidents of this kind, including harm to religious sites, and will continue to act decisively to maintain security and public order in the ​area," the military said. Palestinian officials ​said settlers had also ⁠tried to burn a mosque near Kour, southeast of the city of Tulkarm. Farid Jiyousi, a member of the village council, said three settlers had tried to set the mosque ablaze at dawn ​but worshippers had put out the fire before it reached the main area of the ​mosque. "This is the ⁠first attack our village has experienced," he said, adding that the attackers had also sprayed graffiti in Hebrew on the mosque walls. Following Friday's incident, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces an election in October, ordered a reinforcement of troops in the area and ⁠said ​more settlements would be authorised to increase security. Right-wing politicians in his government, including ​the hardline finance minister Bezalel Smotrich, have called for accelerated moves to take over the West Bank, which was occupied by Israel following the 1967 Middle ​East war. articles.body: Summary Vehicle rammed into crowd, killing one and injuring others Manhunt launched for one or more possible perpetrators Police name one Islamist suspect, ask for public's help Eight seriously wounded, three in life-threatening condition Many details remain unclear BERLIN, July 26 (Reuters) - Germany's government pledged to bring to justice those responsible for Saturday night's deadly attack near a ‌Pride event in Berlin, as police asked the public to help them track down a suspect they identified as an Islamist. A white vehicle ploughed into a crowd in the Tiergarten park near the city's Brandenburg Gate at about 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) not far from one of Europe's biggest annual LGBTQ Pride celebrations, ​Christopher Street Day. One person was killed and 16 injured, eight seriously, emergency services said. Get a look at the day ahead in European and global markets with the Morning Bid Europe newsletter. Sign up here. "This cowardly, despicable attack on people celebrating ​peacefully has shaken me to my core," Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said in a statement. "We will do ⁠everything to quickly investigate this horrific act and what lies behind it and bring those responsible to justice." BERLIN POLICE HUNT SUSPECT IDENTIFIED ​AS KNOWN ISLAMIST Berlin police said overnight they had identified a suspect who was previously known to them and part of the "Islamist spectrum", later naming ​him as Abdul B and publishing his picture. They called on members of the public to help find him. "Who can share anything about his current whereabouts?" a police statement posted online said, describing him as slim, around 1.90 m (6 foot 2 inches) tall, with black hair, and last seen wearing a black hooded top ​and white trousers. It was not clear whether the perpetrator acted alone. Police said more than one person may have got out of the ​vehicle after it came to a halt. Of the 16 people who were injured in the attack, some had suffered stab wounds, the police added. The ‌fire service ⁠said three of the injured were in a life-threatening condition. While the police described the white vehicle involved in the attack only vaguely as possibly a car or minivan or minibus, tabloid newspaper Bild said it was a white Citroen Space Tourer delivery vehicle that Abdul B rented himself. Bild reported that police were also searching for ​a second suspected attacker, but that ​was not confirmed in the ⁠latest police updates. "According to our latest information, the vehicle drove ... into the Tiergarten around 10 p.m., injuring several people in the process, and then came to a standstill after hitting a tree here in the ​Tiergarten," a police spokesperson at the scene said overnight. "It was empty, which is why we are ​currently working intensively ⁠to track down the perpetrator or perpetrators." MERZ GOVERNMENT UNDER PRESSURE BEFORE ELECTIONS The attack comes at a sensitive time for conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz's unpopular coalition government, which is going through a bruising cabinet reshuffle as critics accuse it of being ineffective. State elections are due in two months, with the ⁠far-right opposition ​party Alternative for Germany (AfD) campaigning on issues including immigration and security in a ​bid to secure leadership of a state government for the first time. The AfD was quick to comment on the attack. "We will not allow religious extremists to divide our country ​with violence and intolerance!" AfD co-chief Tino Chrupalla said on X. The U.S. military said on Saturday its naval blockade against Iran "remains in full effect" but did not explain why it halted a streak of 13 nights of escalating strikes. Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up here. There were also no weekend reports of attacks by Iran on neighbors, similar to its daily rejoinders to the U.S. attacks. Asked about the pause, a senior official in ​President Donald Trump 's administration said Trump "has always been clear that his preference is diplomacy, but he has shown Iran what will happen if they fail to come ​to the table in a serious way." Trump has decided, for now, to back away from plans to ramp up attacks on Iran, ⁠the New York Times said on Saturday, citing two people briefed on the discussion. The president and his advisers, the newspaper said, have concerns about expanding the conflict, depleting ​defense stockpiles, alienating Middle East Gulf allies and affecting energy supplies and the global economy. Vice President JD Vance and Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, ​both raised concerns about the U.S. munitions stockpile with Trump during a White House meeting on Friday, a U.S. official told CNN. Operations are "on a hold," a Department of Defense source told the broadcaster on Saturday. Despite the Gulf lull, Saturday's fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia showed that the war, which has already disrupted energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, could affect a second major ​shipping route and reignite Yemen's civil war . Separately, Iran's Foreign Ministry accused Ukraine of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, saying one sailor was killed and another injured. The ​ministry summoned Ukraine's chargé d'affaires in Tehran to protest over an attack it described as "hostile and criminal", state news agency IRNA said. The Iranian denunciation coincided with comments by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy that Kyiv had ‌noted Russia ⁠was passing on to Iran its satellite observations in the Middle East, to enable it to direct strikes in the region. WAR THREATENS TO SPREAD TO YEMEN Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group struck sites belonging to Saudi state oil company Aramco in the cities of Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday. A large column of smoke rose from the direction of the Aramco refinery in Jizan, near the Yemeni border, video on social media verified by Reuters showed. The refinery can process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil ​daily. Two Asia-based trading sources said they had been ​informed of potential damage to fuel ⁠and oil storage sites at Jizan. Aramco (2222.SE) , opens new tab did not respond to requests for comment. In Yanbu, two missiles aimed at oil installations were intercepted. Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea oil port, has become a key route for Saudi oil skirting the Strait of Hormuz, ​which Iran has blockaded. SAUDI-LED COALITION STRIKES HODEIDAH In Yemen, officials said the air force of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, which has ​opposed the Houthis for ⁠more than a decade, struck Houthi sites in the Marib and al-Jawf provinces. The officials said both sides in Yemen's civil war were mobilising forces along the front. Saudi Arabia has led an Arab coalition battling the Houthis since the Iran-aligned fighters captured Yemen's capital, Sanaa. The civil war, in which famine and fighting killed hundreds of thousands, has been paused by a ceasefire since ⁠2022. But that ​truce broke down this month, with the Houthis effectively joining the wider war their Iranian allies have ​waged since being attacked by the United States and Israel five months ago. The Houthis have declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia over the past week, and Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi said all Saudi oil ​facilities could be targets. articles.body: CAIRO, July 25 (Reuters) - An Israeli airstrike on Saturday killed the head of the Hamas-led police force in the northern Gaza Strip, Brigadier-General Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the group-run interior ministry and ​medics said. Medics and the interior ministry said Maqadma, known also as the governor ‌of northern Gaza Strip, was killed by an Israeli airstrike in the Sheikh Radwan area north of Gaza City. The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up here. In a separate incident, another Israeli strike killed a Palestinian medic in the Nuseirat refugee camp in ​central Gaza Strip, medics said. They added that a police officer, wounded by an ​Israeli airstrike last week, died on Saturday. The Israeli military did not immediately ⁠comment on any of the incidents. Israel has killed dozens of members of the Hamas-led police force , opens new tab , ​including senior officials, in the past months, accusing many of them of being members of the ​Hamas armed wing who posed imminent threats to Israel and its forces inside Gaza. Hamas says Israeli attacks on the police force and its headquarters are intended to sow chaos and anarchy in the enclave and violate ​the U.S.-brokered October ceasefire . The latest deaths add to a toll of more than 1,180 Palestinians, mostly ​civilians, killed by Israeli attacks since an October ceasefire between Israel and Hamas militants took effect, according to ‌Gaza ⁠health officials. Hamas does not usually disclose its losses. The truce halted full-scale fighting but has not ended near-daily Israeli strikes. Four Israeli soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period. Mediators including Egypt, Qatar, Turkey and the United States have been trying to advance U.S. ​President Donald Trump's plan ​for ending the ⁠conflict in Gaza, which calls for Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawals, but there has been little sign of progress in the efforts. The war began ​when Hamas-led fighters attacked southern Israel, killing 1,200 people and taking ​about 250 ⁠hostages, according to Israeli tallies. Israel's subsequent offensive has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians, say Gaza health officials. Israel effectively controls an estimated 64% of the tiny coastal Strip, bombarded to ruins by Israel's ⁠two-year ​military assault that followed the 2023 Hamas attack on ​southern Israel. Nearly all of Gaza's 2 million people now live on a tiny strip of land, mainly in makeshift tents ​or damaged buildings and facing dire conditions , under Hamas control. articles.body: Summary Blazes moving inland towards France's ninth city Flames now 30 km from Bordeaux, suburbs cleared Of three fires near Madrid, two have merged Spain awaiting water-dumping aircraft from abroad Spanish minister warns against outside activity BORDEAUX, France/MADRID, July 25 (Reuters) - Wildfires on the coast of southwestern France moved inland towards Bordeaux on Saturday, forcing the evacuation of thousands in the ‌city's suburbs, while in neighbouring Spain high winds complicated efforts to fight a massive blaze near Madrid. Hundreds of thousands of people have been evacuated in both countries because of those fires, the latest natural disasters linked to sustained dry spells and successive heatwaves that scientists say have been exacerbated by climate change. Stay up to date on the key companies, data, and decisions in the ESG world with the Reuters Sustainable Finance newsletter. Sign up here. "The fires that ​are hitting our country have reached a level that has never been seen before," French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu wrote on ​X. "We expect a fight that will be long and very difficult," Interior Minister Laurent Nunez later told reporters, adding ⁠that Bordeaux airport had been closed. France's armed forces have been drafted in to help overwhelmed fire brigades, while Spain has declared its first national ​emergency over a wildfire, because of three blazes, two of which merged on Friday. Spain's Civil Protection Service said it was expecting four more ​water-dumping aircraft to arrive on Saturday, two from Italy and two from Greece - sent as part of a European Union response to the emergency. Firefighting aircraft from the Netherlands and Portugal have already been deployed in Spain. High winds have stoked and spread the fires in both countries. The coast near Bordeaux is a tourist hotspot which ​includes pine forests that can catch fire easily. The city is also famous for its eponymous wines, made by nearby vineyards. Roughly 197,000 people ​have so far been evacuated from the Gironde and Landes regions close to Bordeaux since the wildfires broke out there this week. More than 63,000 people ‌have been ⁠evacuated or confined to their homes in Spain because of the three major fires there. The government has warned against road or rail travel to the area. SPAIN WARNS AGAINST GOING OUTSIDE Many Madrid residents have second homes in the densely ​populated area west of the capital ​but still in the region ⁠of Madrid where the two fires merged. A third fire in Avila province has threatened to merge with the two in Madrid, Nicanor Sen, the government representative for the Castile and Leon region, told reporters on Friday. Esteban ​Carrasco, owner of the Monasterio de Pelayos campsite west of the capital, told national broadcaster TVE about ​30 mobile homes ⁠were burned down when the fire reached the site on Friday. About 200 campers from "humble backgrounds" had to evacuate, he added. "It was a horrific disaster," he said as he showed how mobile homes on one side of a road were destroyed while on the other side they escaped untouched. No ⁠one was ​injured. While smoke filled the air in Madrid on Friday, it was clearer on Saturday ​but Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia still warned against outdoor activities. "Avoid physical activity and staying outdoors. If you go outdoors and there is smoke or ash, use a mask," she ​said on X. Purchase Licensing Rights , opens new tab Read more Summary Netanyahu orders crackdown after West Bank shooting incident Palestinians say shootout provoked by armed settlers Social media footage shows confused confrontation RAMALLAH, July 25 (Reuters) - Israeli forces arrested dozens of Palestinians in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, after at least four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers ​were killed in a shootout when armed Israeli settlers approached a Palestinian village. Palestinian authorities in the West Bank said ‌Friday's shootings were provoked by the settlers who aimed to attack villagers in Tal, southwest of Nablus. The Israeli military initially described the Israeli civilians involved in the incident as hikers, but later acknowledged some were armed and said both sides had opened fire before troops intervened. The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up here. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to take "powerful ​action" in response to the incident, including demolishing the home of the family of one of the Palestinians involved. Netanyahu's ​office said he would accelerate the approval of construction of more Israeli settlements in the area. Walid Zidan, ⁠the mayor of Tal, said around 70 people from the village had been detained and questioned at a field interrogation centre set up ​in a house in the village. Around 10 to 12 had been released so far, he told Reuters by telephone. "House raids are continuing, ​army patrols are driving through the streets, and there is no movement of people in the streets," he said. Hundreds of thousands of Israeli settlers live among millions of Palestinians in the West Bank, which Israel captured in a war in 1967. Nearly all countries and UN bodies consider such settlements illegal under international ​law. Israel disputes this, citing biblical and historical ties to the land. Recent months have seen a sharp increase in attacks by Israeli settlers ​on Palestinian villages. Friday's incident took place in the so-called "area A" of the West Bank, where Palestinian authorities have administrative control and Israeli civilians are barred under ‌Israeli ⁠law from entering. Area A comprises less than a fifth of the West Bank. Footage circulating on social media of the incident that led to Friday's shootout appeared to show a confused standoff between a crowd of villagers and a large group of Israelis, at least some of them armed, with soldiers also visible. At one point, at least two Israelis are seen pushing and hitting Palestinians with the stocks of their ​rifles, before one of the Palestinians ​seizes one of the weapons ⁠and is then apparently shot dead. In the background, voices can be heard shouting in Hebrew "Get away," "He's trying to snatch his weapon. He's snatched his weapon," and "Shoot him!" A child's voice is heard shouting "Revenge!" Reuters has ​not been able to authenticate the footage independently. CONFRONTATION Israel's army chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir said the security ​operation launched after ⁠the shootings was intended "to thwart terrorism, ensure the security of Israeli civilians and prevent further escalation". Zidan, the mayor, said the incident had been triggered by Israeli settlers deliberately harassing the village. "The settlers were not following a route or trail, as they claim. They intended to attack the homes," ⁠Zidan said. "People ​did not go there looking for a confrontation with them; they were simply defending ​their homes, nothing more and nothing less." The sharp increase in settler attacks on Palestinian villages in the West Bank seen in recent months has drawn condemnation from international agencies and ​countries in Europe but has done little to reverse the trend. Wildberries said ​it had temporarily halted operations at the Yekaterinburg facility for security reasons, but that the ​site had not been damaged. Around four hours later, it said operations had ⁠resumed. Earlier on Saturday, local authorities declared a drone alert over the wider Sverdlovsk region and said ​one attack had been repelled over Yekaterinburg, Russia's fourth-largest city. Falling drone debris set fire to a ​parking lot, Governor Denis Pasler wrote on the Telegram app. "Economic and infrastructure facilities were not damaged," he said, cautioning residents to remain vigilant as the drone threat persisted. The alert also delayed the penultimate day of competition at the ​Russian Athletics Championships, which the city was hosting. Athletes and spectators had to leave the open stadium ​and take shelter, according to a Reuters witness. "This has never happened to me at competitions, but in everyday life ‌it ⁠has. Sometimes, even during training, we'll have drone alerts and sirens going off. So, it's a normal atmosphere, so to speak," said runner Anastasia Fedonina from the southwestern Volgograd region. Ukraine has stepped up long-range drone attacks on Russian infrastructure this year in a bid to undermine its war effort and ​pressure the Kremlin to make ​peace. It says it ⁠has targeted Wildberries on the grounds that it handles military supplies, which the Kremlin has denied. Since launching its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, ​Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukrainian logistics infrastructure, as well as its energy system ​and power ⁠grid. On Saturday, local authorities in Russia's southern Krasnodar region said open flames had been extinguished at a warehouse hit by drones on Wednesday. They did not name the facility, but a Wildberries warehouse in Krasnodar ⁠was ​attacked that day. Together with smaller rivals, Wildberries and top competitor ​Ozon sell goods and services worth the equivalent of 8.5% of Russia's gross domestic product and employ 4 million people, or ​more than 5% of the country's workforce. REUTERS/Ammar Awad Purchase Licensing Rights , opens new tab RAMALLAH, West Bank, July 25 (Reuters) - Palestinian officials welcomed UNESCO's designation of Sebastia in the occupied West Bank as a World Heritage site, hoping it will prevent Israel extending ​its control at the ancient village, while Israel condemned it as a political ‌decision. Sebastia, in the northern West Bank, has archaeological remnants from successive periods dating back at least to the 9th-century BC capital of the Israelite kingdom, through the Hellenistic, Roman, Byzantine, Islamic periods, Crusader and Ottoman ​eras, according to UNESCO, the United Nations cultural organisation. The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up here. Olive trees surround the site, dotting ​a landscape of Roman columns, ancient walls and stone steps and an ⁠amphitheatre. It is traditionally seen as the burial place of John the Baptist. But Palestinian residents ​of the adjacent village, many of whom rely on tourism for a living, are facing ​land confiscations after Israel announced a plan to seize about 1,800 dunams (445 acres) at the site, which it said was meant to develop the area. On Friday, UNESCO added Sebastia to its World Heritage List and to the ​List of World Heritage in Danger, a related mechanism used to flag listed heritage sites ​that are facing serious threats, to try and safeguard them. "We hope that this decision will enable us ‌to preserve ⁠Sebastia," said Nizar Kayed, the village deputy mayor. He said that Israel's land seizure decision, announced in late 2025, was part of an Israeli push to expand settlements in the area. The Palestinian tourism and foreign ministries said on Friday that they hoped the UNESCO recognition would ​help mobilize international support ​against Israeli measures ⁠there. Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said the UNESCO decision was part of a Palestinian drive to obscure Jewish ties to the land. "No vote ​in an international organization can change history," he said in a statement. Palestinian ​officials are ⁠also concerned about a new Israeli bill , that has yet to be written into law, that would extend Israeli civil control over ancient sites in the West Bank. That in effect would strip away ⁠oversight of ​the ancient sites from the Western-backed Palestinian Authority, which ​under the 1990s Oslo peace accords has exercised limited self-rule in parts of the West Bank, territory Israel captured ​in a 1967 war. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights , opens new tab Summary New forced-labor duties of 10% or 12.5% cover 99.4% of U.S. imports, USTR said Greer said rebuilt tariff layers will not exceed caps in negotiated trade deals The latest actions include probes into excess capacity and alleged Vietnamese intellectual property theft WASHINGTON, July 25 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump had no time for lengthy tariff investigations when he returned to office last year, wanting to hammer trading partners right away to wring concessions. What followed was a chaotic start to a ​trade agenda that was eventually upended by a stinging Supreme Court defeat this year. Now he and his team are moving into a new phase to build a more durable U.S. tariff wall using ‌more traditional and court-tested trade laws, those he had little patience for 18 months ago. Jumpstart your morning with the latest legal news delivered straight to your inbox from The Daily Docket newsletter. Sign up here. His latest global tariff salvo — duties of 10% or 12.5% on 60 countries over allegedly weak enforcement of forced-labor bans — marks the first of numerous tariff actions to be unveiled in the months ahead. They include probes into excess industrial capacity, alleged intellectual property theft by Vietnam, and national security protections for strategic industries from semiconductors to robotics and industrial machinery. "We're at the end of the beginning of the Trump tariff agenda," said Dan Ujczo, associate general counsel at Canadian oil producer Cenovus ​Energy, who specializes in U.S.-Canada trade. "Within the next few weeks, and certainly by the end of the summer, we will see large parts of President Trump's trade policy fully in effect." This could bring more clarity and certainty ​for businesses on Trump's ultimate tariff structure, along with dread in foreign trade ministries that they may have to cough up more concessions to protect access to a $3.4 trillion U.S. ⁠import market. DIRECT REPLACEMENTS Trump's new anti-forced labor duties imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, the unfair trade practices statute used against China during his first term, almost directly replace a global 10% temporary tariff that expired on Friday. ​They cover 99.4% of U.S. imports, the U.S. Trade Representative's office said. This rebuilds part of Trump's signature "Liberation Day" tariffs of 10%-50% on nearly every country, which the U.S. Supreme Court struck down as illegal under an untested national emergencies law Trump used ​to impose them. Another part of the baseline tariffs is likely to be rebuilt by another Section 301 investigation into excess industrial capacity , targeting 16 big trading partners, including China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Mexico and Vietnam. That ongoing probe targets industrial subsidies and other export-focused policies. Amid a wider uproar over Trump's move, some viewed it as largely maintaining the status quo. Mark Bissell, CEO of Michigan-based vacuum maker Bissell Inc, said the newest tariffs were largely what the company anticipated and it hadn`t frontloaded inventory from China and elsewhere to try to beat them. "We continued to run ​the business based on the belief that the tariffs would stay in the 10-15% range," Bissell said in an email to Reuters. BUDGET IMPACT Trump's gamble on quick but untested tariffs right out of the gate did four things. It heaped added costs ​onto retailers and other import-dependent industries; it brought dozens of trading partners to the negotiating table, yielding concessions for lower rates; it prompted swift retaliation and tariff escalation from China that led to a delicate truce; and it filled U.S. fiscal coffers with hundreds of ‌billions of dollars. ⁠The Liberation Day tariffs alone yielded $166 billion in revenue, a major offset to a growing federal deficit, but refunds to importers have now turned those collections negative. The 150-day temporary tariffs, based on a law meant to quell balance-of-payments crises, have added $31 billion in assessed revenue through July 5. But if a federal court ruling against them stands, that money, too, is subject to refund. With U.S. public debt approaching $40 trillion, Josh Lipsky, chair of international economics at the Atlantic Council, said subsequent administrations may become addicted to tariff revenue that is likely to be sustained. "The tariff wall is being rebuilt strong brick by strong brick, and it's very durable," Lipsky said. Trump's broad use of Section 301 in the forced-labor case prompted an immediate legal challenge by small businesses, but trade and ​legal experts say this will take time to play out. ​The statute has a solid track record in the ⁠courts, and judges may be reluctant to enjoin actions aimed at curbing forced labor and lowering barriers to U.S. goods. MORE TO COME U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer made clear this week that Trump will use everything at his disposal to erect tariffs to reshore production and shrink the trade deficit. "The specific authorities this administration is using have changed, but the trade strategy has not," ​Greer told the U.S. Senate Finance Committee. Greer, who has not committed to a timeline for the industrial capacity investigations, has said the layers of tariffs being rebuilt will not ​exceed caps included in deals he ⁠has been negotiating, including 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea and higher rates for Southeast Asian countries. Administration officials say even though China is viewed as the world's largest source of excess manufacturing, its rates will not exceed the cap of about 20% agreed by Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping last November, which is on top of the 25% tariffs from his first term. Some nominal — or announced — duties may be higher than actual applied rates, which analysts say may be an enforcement mechanism for countries to stick ⁠to agreed trade ​deal terms. Still, some things continue to come out of the blue, including the 50% duties on Canadian beer, dairy, hockey sticks and other products Trump ​announced on Monday over Ottawa's refusal to make trade concessions, and his threat to cut off all trade with Spain over not meeting NATO military spending targets. That proclivity for spontaneous tariff announcements remains an ongoing risk, said Eswar Prasad, a trade professor at Cornell University and former head of the International ​Monetary Fund's China department. "Trump`s eagerness to impose tariffs to address a whole range of grievances will not only continue disrupting the global trading system but will have significant adverse effects on American households and businesses." articles.body: BANGOR, Maine — Republicans had months to research and rebuke Graham Platner. They now have exactly 100 days to sink his replacement. Troy Jackson is like Platner but worse. He’s a socialist who’s flip-flopped on policy, a career politician who keeps losing, an insider who is also unknown. His nomination was illegitimate, he has anger issues, and he lacks “rizz.” That’s just a sampling of the messaging the GOP plans to use to trounce Jackson, the former Maine Senate president who lost this year’s Democratic gubernatorial primary only to glide this weekend into the party’s nomination to challenge Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) in November. “Mainers already rejected Troy Jackson once this year after his failed campaign for governor. Now Democrats are asking voters to believe the politician they didn’t want leading Augusta belongs in the United States Senate,” the NRSC, Senate Republicans’ campaign arm, wrote in a “messaging guidance” document about Jackson, viewed by Playbook. “Jackson is a radical, ill-tempered career politician whose failed record and socialist agenda make him unfit to represent Maine.” The stakes are high. Collins is the only Republican senator running for re-election this cycle in a state Kamala Harris won in 2024, and Democrats’ hopes of retaking the chamber track straight through Maine — a reality the NRSC admitted is possible in its new donor memo , shared first with Playbook, acknowledging that “Jackson is fully capable of winning this seat if we become complacent.” Republicans’ first plan of attack is to link Jackson to Platner, with whom he campaigned and shares much of his populist platform. As soon as Jackson’s nomination became official yesterday, the Senate Leadership Fund, the Senate GOP’s super PAC, announced that it was launching a six-figure ad blitz that begins by depicting the two Democrats hugging on stage. “Jackson is like Graham Platner but worse,” the ad says, citing reporting from WaPo , CNN and other outlets about Jackson’s alleged sharp temper and heated interactions with colleagues. The NRSC yesterday posted a video on X depicting Platner literally transforming into Jackson — with the caption “No tattoo, same crazy,” a reference to Platner’s tattoo that resembled a Nazi symbol. “Troy Jackson is all the baggage without the ‘rizz,” James Blair, who leads President Donald Trump’s outside political operation, said on X . Jackson campaigned alongside Platner and stood by him through several scandals — until POLITICO reported earlier this month that a woman who dated Platner said he had sexually assaulted her, a claim Platner denies. In response, Jackson publicly disavowed Platner and said he had “lied to me.” Jackson told reporters yesterday he has not spoken to Platner since then. Asked to respond to SLF’s ad, Jackson said “anyone that I may have argued with, that I might have went too far or got too passionate, I apologize to.” The GOP’s second push is to brand Jackson as a “political insider” — a bid to undermine his populist bonafides at a time when voters from neither party trust establishment politicians. “We must act immediately to define him before national Democrats frame him as a populist outsider,” the NRSC memo said. “Chuck Schumer forcefully removed Graham Platner from the ballot against the will of Maine voters, only to replace him with a deranged and scandal-plagued political insider,” SLF Communications Director Chris Gustafson said in a statement to POLITICO. Part of that strategy is to not only label Jackson as a longserving member of the establishment (Collins, for what it’s worth, has held her seat for nearly three decades), but as a political insider who has failed when seeking higher office. As state Senate president, Jackson was the second-highest ranking official in Maine — but he ran unsuccessfully for the Democratic nomination for Congress in 2014 and for governor earlier this year, a fresh wound Republicans are eager to pick at. Compounding that insider image is the way Maine Democrats selected Jackson: While more than 200,000 Mainers voted for Platner in the primary, just 566 Democratic delegates actively chose Jackson at yesterday’s nominating convention — a fact Republicans hope to spin into a narrative that Jackson was coronated by party insiders. “Not one single vote was cast for Troy Jackson” in the Senate race, RNC Chair Joe Gruters said on X . “Just one month ago, Troy came in third in the Democratic primary for Governor. Now he will run for Senate as the third choice of his party insiders,” Collins campaign spokesperson Shawn Roderick said in a statement to Playbook. He added, “in a process concocted by the Maine Democratic Party establishment, a 24-year Augusta insider was appointed to run for the Senate by fewer than three-tenths of one percent of its primary voters.” Jackson, for his part, appears committed to maintaining his image as a populist who, as has become his campaign motto, comes neither from the left nor the right, but “from the bottom.” He’s more eager to bring up being a fifth-generation logger than his decades of experience in state politics — and at any mention of his relationship to Platner, he’s quick to pivot to his role as part of a broader pro-worker movement. And his campaign is staying laser-focused on attacking Collins . “Only Susan Collins could spend nearly 30 years in Washington voting with Donald Trump 96 percent of the time and taking millions from corporate special interests, then call a fifth-generation logger from Allagash a ‘party insider,’” Jackson campaign adviser BJ McCollister said in a statement to Playbook. “Mainers know who Troy Jackson is—and they know exactly who Susan Collins works for.” Asked yesterday to respond to the GOP messaging shortly after clinching the official nomination, Jackson told reporters that he attributes Republicans’ attacks to “Senator Collins trying to make sure that she can win re-election on a really bad record.” “I've been in the legislature for 20 years,” he added. “I do believe I've been vetted. I've been tested. People know exactly what I'm fighting for. They know that I've had their back, and they know they can trust me.” Andrew Howard contributed to this report.
articles.headline: How Republicans plan to conquer Troy Jackson

articles.body: McALLEN, Texas — Just miles from the U.S.-Mexico border, Ken Paxton is trying to inherit President Donald Trump’s historic gains with Hispanic voters. The Texas GOP Senate nominee, speaking to hundreds of supporters last week at his first campaign rally in this region that’s almost entirely Latino, revealed how Republicans believe that’s possible: by touting Trump’s closure of the border and hitting Democrats over the head with the culture war — while ignoring the drag his mass deportations have had on the region. The GOP faithful, clad in signature MAGA red and a few scattered Trump 2028 hats, gathered at a beer hall outdoors in 100-degree heat to greet the Republican Senate nominee and other candidates. Attendees ate up the Republicans’ constant jabs at Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico. Eric Flores, the challenger to Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez, called Talarico a “low T.” Paxton belittled Talarico, a seminarian student and critic of Christian nationalism, for referring to himself as a “Christian who hates Christianity.” It’s an approach key to Paxton’s strategy, as Republican Senate nominee, to slice into Talarico’s widening polling lead with Hispanic voters, who could prove decisive for who wins the competitive Senate seat and a litany of other races that will determine which party takes power in Washington come November. “Once this community knows what [Talarico’s] views are on transitioning boys into girls, and girls into boys, and boys and girls sports, they're not going to support it,” Paxton told reporters after the rally, in response to a question of how he intends to keep Hispanic voters in the fold after they swung toward Trump in 2024. This has worked before for the Texas GOP. Sen. Ted Cruz blitzed the airways in the 2024 Senate race with attack ads against former Rep. Colin Allred about transgender youth participation in sports. Republicans branded Wendy Davis “ abortion Barbie ” following her successful protest against an anti-abortion law in the state legislature. But outside the carefully choreographed event is a community getting pummelled by the president’s increasingly unpopular immigration agenda — a reality that’s given Democrats a strong opening with Latinos as they attempt to end a decades-long losing streak in statewide races. Interviews with local lawmakers, business leaders and voters on both sides of the aisle reveal that Democratic candidates like Talarico and gubernatorial nominee Gina Hinojosa have so far been successful at appealing to Hispanic voters feeling the economic strain under Trump. Talarico, who appeared in McAllen for an event 16 hours after Paxton’s, kept his pitch focused on the cost of living, handing out hot plates of food and calling for a reversal in health care cuts under the GOP budget bill enacted last year. “He's pretty steady and focused on the issues that matter to families,” said Democratic state Sen. Juan Hinojosa, whose district spans Corpus Christi to McAllen. “Democrats get sidetracked on all these cultural issues, and they need to stay focused on what I call the bread butter issues, issues that impact families directly, the kitchen table issues,” he said. “Democrats need to stay away from biting the hook that's being put out by Paxton.” A community being squeezed The Rio Grande Valley is buckling under the weight of Trump’s policies, and the economic strain is visible in McAllen. Deportations have dried up workforces in critical industries like construction that drive the local economy, leaving cement slabs half-poured. A traffic chokehold at the border has slowed business in retail and restaurants as Mexicans have been deterred from hopping over to the U.S. for the day. The entire border is being squeezed. Laredo, located more than 150 miles from McAllen, is one of the nation’s top trade hubs, and its leaders are warning that Trump’s tariffs and his threat to eliminate the USMCA trade agreement stands to devastate international commerce that flows through the city. “When the U.S. doesn't provide economic opportunity for the people at the border, it will create this situation,” said Laredo Mayor Victor D. Treviño, a Democrat, in an interview. The Paxton campaign dismissed concerns of Democrats’ gains with Latinos, especially in the Rio Grande Valley — and once again emphasized the culture war, which Republicans say resonates with socially conservative Latinos. "Look, Hispanic families aren't voting for a woke vegan who says God is nonbinary and wants to Latinx our children,” said Alex Alarcon, director of Hispanic outreach for the Paxton campaign, in a statement. “We're proud of our culture and our faith, and Ken Paxton has spent his career fighting for us: a secure border to protect our families, a cost of living we can actually afford, and the freedom to live by our values.” Still, the tide seems to be turning toward Democrats. A dozen residents along the border said in interviews that they are satisfied illegal border crossings have dropped to record lows, a realization of one of Trump’s top campaign promises and one of the reasons he won over Hispanic voters in the region. But they also believe the crackdown has gone too far. More than 60 percent of Hispanics said Trump’s mass deportations campaign — including his widespread deployment of ICE agents across the U.S. — has been too aggressive, according to a July POLITICO Poll. In McAllen last week, the community was still aghast over a nun who was recently arrested by ICE while walking to church. She was later released after GOP Rep. Monica De La Cruz and Democrat Rep. Henry Cuellar intervened, but interviews with residents revealed they still live in fear: Even U.S. citizens are checking their pockets for ID before venturing out, and they try to steer clear of the border if possible. Across Texas, one in five Hispanic business owners said they’ve had an employee deported in the past year and 70 percent have been impacted by Trump’s tariffs, according to a June survey commissioned by the U.S. Hispanic Business Council and shared first with POLITICO . Talarico holds a seven-point lead over Paxton among those surveyed — even though a plurality of them self-identified as Republican. A national Republican close to the race, granted anonymity to speak freely, countered that Paxton stands to benefit from some of the most competitive House races taking place in South Texas — where Republican Tano Tijerina and Flores are trying to oust Reps. Henry Cuellar and Gonzalez, respectively, and Rep. Monica De La Cruz is fending off a challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido. GOP campaigns have stood up multiple field centers in those districts drawn to favor Republicans under a new Congressional map, a ground game that is expected to boost Paxton at the top of the ticket, the person said. They added that internal message testing shows some of the attacks on Talarico, specifically those regarding his past comments on gender, "is unlike anything we've ever seen with Hispanic men, just in terms of the amount that it moves them." Daniel Garza, president of the LIBRE Initiative, a grassroots conservative group based in South Texas, said Trump’s closure of the border has affirmed Hispanic’s support for him, and Democrats aren’t offering viable pro-growth economic plans. “Democrats have failed to give Latino voters something to vote for, and that they've only focused solely on something you know for us to vote against. And that's not good enough,” he said. “[Latinos] want less tax burden, less regulatory burden, more energy production.” Talarico’s pitch to Hispanics Talarico was also in McAllen, just one day after Paxon’s rally, to host a fundraising benefit — the final stop on a 750-mile bus tour hitting small towns along the border to deliver a message about lowering costs and creating jobs. In an attempt to cast himself as a tough-on-immigration Democrat, Talarico unveiled a border security plan that includes hiring more Border Patrol agents, a major employer in South Texas, and adding immigration judges to reduce the asylum backlog. It’s part of his attempt to widen his current edge over Paxton with Hispanics, with a New York Times poll in June showing Talarico is winning the demographic by a 61 percent to 29 percent margin — a significant shift after Trump won 55 percent of Hispanic voters in Texas in 2024. “You could drive a truck through the margin of error on the Times’ subsample,” Alarcon, Paxton’s Hispanic outreach director, said. “The fact is nobody is winning Hispanic voters by default this cycle. We’ll be in Spanish-language media from the Valley to Dallas, talking about groceries, gas, health care and a secure border.” Still, Talarico’s lead has given Democratic party leaders hope amid their national tug-of-war with Republicans over Hispanic voters: If Talarico can hold onto Texas’ large Latino population by these margins through November, that would prove gradual gains over the past decade for Republicans were a temporary blip ahead of the 2028 presidential race. Under the midday sweltering sun in McAllen, Talarico handed out hot plates of food to a line of people who had donated to a local woman struggling to pay for cancer treatment. The Democratic Senate nominee, while speaking to reporters later, dismissed Paxton’s attempts to appeal to Hispanic voters by making personal attacks against him. Republicans are attempting to divide people, Talarico said, “so we don't notice that they're picking our pockets, that they're closing our public schools, that they're gutting our health care, that they're raising taxes on working people while they cut taxes for billionaires. It's the oldest strategy in the world.” Talarico’s campaign is leaning hard into its outreach to the Hispanic community, including efforts like running a Spanish-language ad during the World Cup talking about his background as a teacher, plans to defend Medicaid and social security, and push to raise taxes on billionaires. He also ran an ad during the Mexico vs. Panama soccer match and launched a Spanish-language social media channel. Local Democratic party officials have begun targeted organizing efforts to turn out Hispanic voters throughout the Rio Grande Valley. But the challenge, they say, is convincing Hispanics running away from Republicans to instead run toward Democrats and not stay home in November. Democrats are heartened by an uptick in primary turnout in the region, which in March saw more than double the number of primary voters than in 2024. Trump carried all four counties in the RGV that year, the first time in history a Republican has won them at the presidential level, but Democrats won at every level down ballot. “We're hoping to carry that momentum,” said Hidalgo County Democratic chair Richard Gonzales, referring to the high primary turnout. “Republicans beat us because they made it seem like they could solve the problems. They got in and then they just created more problems.” CORRECTION: This article has been updated to better reflect Eric Flores' remarks at a campaign rally in McAllen, Texas, about Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico.

articles.body: <p>La semana que ahora acaba tenía señalada una fecha importante en el calendario del <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/plus-ultra/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/plus-ultra/"><i>caso Plus Ultra</i></a>, en el que está investigado José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero por, supuestamente, liderar una red de influencias ilícitas que, entre otras operaciones, favoreció el rescate público en 2021 de la aerolínea que da nombre a la causa. El juez José Luis Calama había citado para el martes como investigado a Julio Martínez Martínez, amigo del expresidente del Gobierno y administrador de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-05-19/analisis-relevante-la-empresa-clave-en-el-caso-plus-ultra-que-implica-a-zapatero.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-05-19/analisis-relevante-la-empresa-clave-en-el-caso-plus-ultra-que-implica-a-zapatero.html">Análisis Relevante, la empresa en el epicentro de la trama</a>. La cita se presumía determinante ante la duda de si el empresario respaldaría la versión de Zapatero, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-17/zapatero-declara-ante-el-juez-para-defender-su-inocencia-en-medio-de-una-gran-presion-politica-para-el-gobierno.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-17/zapatero-declara-ante-el-juez-para-defender-su-inocencia-en-medio-de-una-gran-presion-politica-para-el-gobierno.html">que declaró en junio y aseguró que era ajeno a la creación y administración</a> de esa sociedad y solo trabajó y cobró de ella como consultor externo, o si, por el contrario, desmentiría ese relato y corroboraría el de los investigadores, que sitúan al expresidente a los mandos del entramado. Martínez Martínez no esperó a estar ante el juez y, en la víspera de su citación, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-20/el-empresario-julio-martinez-senala-a-zapatero-en-el-rescate-de-plus-ultra.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-20/el-empresario-julio-martinez-senala-a-zapatero-en-el-rescate-de-plus-ultra.html">entregó en la Audiencia Nacional un documento</a> en el que se ofrecía a colaborar con la justicia y señalaba a Zapatero. Comenzó así un movimiento en cadena a<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-22/dos-directivos-de-plus-ultra-ratifican-la-veracidad-de-mensajes-incriminatorios-que-zapatero-intenta-anular.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-22/dos-directivos-de-plus-ultra-ratifican-la-veracidad-de-mensajes-incriminatorios-que-zapatero-intenta-anular.html">l que se sumaron Julio Martínez Sola y Roberto Roselli</a>, también imputados y hasta entonces máximos directivos de la aerolínea Plus Ultra (dimitieron este viernes tras ser citados por el juez), que endosa al exlíder socialista la máxima responsabilidad en los hechos que se investigan.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-26/la-semana-que-dejo-a-zapatero-aislado-en-la-red-de-plus-ultra.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Miércoles 24 de junio, última sesión de control al Gobierno antes del cierre veraniego del Congreso. La corrupción, protagonista. Con desatada velocidad verbal, el portavoz de ERC, Gabriel Rufián, recita un <i>totum revolutum </i>de casos del PP, “la Gürtel, la Lezo, la Púnica, la Kitchen”, para luego jalonar su intervención de nombres bien conocidos: los de dos exministros populares condenados, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/2024-10-15/eduardo-zaplana-condenado-a-10-anos-de-carcel-por-el-cobro-de-mordidas-tras-la-concesion-de-las-itv.html" rel="">Eduardo Zaplana</a> y <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2024-12-20/rodrigo-rato-condenado-a-4-anos-y-nueves-meses-de-prision-por-el-origen-de-su-fortuna.html" rel="">Rodrigo Rato</a>, el de otro que está siendo juzgado, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-24/un-inspector-que-trabajo-para-cospedal-y-el-exchofer-de-barcenas-declaran-este-miercoles-en-el-juicio-de-kitchen.html" rel="">Jorge Fernández Díaz</a>, el de otro que está siendo investigado, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-07-16/cristobal-montoro-imputado-por-crear-una-red-de-influencias-durante-su-primera-etapa-como-ministro-de-hacienda.html" rel="">Cristóbal Montoro</a>, más el de un expresidente madrileño que previsiblemente se sentará el año que viene en el banquillo, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2025-12-22/la-audiencia-nacional-fija-para-septiembre-de-2027-el-juicio-contra-ignacio-gonzalez-por-el-campo-de-golf-del-canal-isabel-ii.html" rel="">Ignacio González</a>. No para de nombrar casos y políticos. “Me falta el aire”, resopla para ilustrar el desafío de repasar los casos de corrupción que afectan al PP.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-26/el-pasado-lastra-la-cruzada-anticorrupcion-del-pp.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

Tras ella, el ministro Marlaska (derecha) y el delegado del Gobierno en la región."></img><p>El amago de bronca<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-24/sanchez-y-marlaska-inciden-en-la-solidaridad-y-puente-acusa-al-pp-de-querer-que-les-resuelvan-la-papeleta-de-los-incendios.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-24/sanchez-y-marlaska-inciden-en-la-solidaridad-y-puente-acusa-al-pp-de-querer-que-les-resuelvan-la-papeleta-de-los-incendios.html"> entre algunos miembros del Gobierno y la Comunidad de Madrid</a> a propósito del <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-25/los-incendios-de-madrid-y-avila-ya-han-calcinado-mas-de-15000-hectareas-y-han-obligado-a-evacuar-o-confinar-a-63000-personas.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-25/los-incendios-de-madrid-y-avila-ya-han-calcinado-mas-de-15000-hectareas-y-han-obligado-a-evacuar-o-confinar-a-63000-personas.html">gran incendio en la sierra sur de la región </a>se acalló este sábado. Pedro Sánchez e Isabel Díaz Ayuso coincidieron a primera hora en la reunión del comité de coordinación de la emergencia celebrada en el puesto de mando de la localidad de Cenicientos, antes de que tuviese que ser desalojado por la proximidad de las llamas. A su llegada, el presidente del Gobierno saludó con frialdad a la jefa de la comunidad madrileña. Luego, Ayuso no quiso comparecer ante los medios junto a Sánchez, según comentaron fuentes de La Moncloa, en contra de lo que sí hicieron en ocasiones similares otros barones del PP <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-13/sanchez-y-moreno-advierten-juntos-sobre-el-cambio-climatico-10-dias-despues-del-acuerdo-entre-el-pp-y-vox.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-13/sanchez-y-moreno-advierten-juntos-sobre-el-cambio-climatico-10-dias-despues-del-acuerdo-entre-el-pp-y-vox.html">como el andaluz Juan Manuel Moreno</a> o el gallego Alfonso Rueda. Pero en las declaraciones no se deslizó el menor reproche entre ambos. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-26/el-gobierno-y-ayuso-aparcan-sus-diferencias-ante-la-magnitud-del-fuego.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Pedro Sánchez estaba noqueado hace un año. El presidente llegó “hundido” al mes de agosto, recuerda uno de sus principales apoyos orgánicos e institucionales. Los<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-22/el-supremo-condena-a-abalos-a-24-anos-y-tres-meses-de-carcel-a-koldo-garcia-a-19-anos-y-ocho-meses-y-a-aldama-a-cuatro-anos-y-medio.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-22/el-supremo-condena-a-abalos-a-24-anos-y-tres-meses-de-carcel-a-koldo-garcia-a-19-anos-y-ocho-meses-y-a-aldama-a-cuatro-anos-y-medio.html"> escándalos de corrupción de José Luis Ábalos y Santos Cerdán</a> y las acusaciones de acoso sexual a Francisco Salazar estuvieron a punto de tumbar al Gobierno: “Todos estábamos abatidos, el ambiente en La Moncloa era depresivo. Pesimismo puro. No teníamos nada claro cuánto iba a durar la legislatura. Ahora ya nadie duda de que lo hará hasta 2027″, asiente un miembro del Ejecutivo. Sánchez llegó a reconocer en el Congreso que se había planteado dimitir. No era la primera vez. En los cinco días de reflexión que se tomó a finales de abril de 2024 por el inicio de la causa judicial contra su esposa ya estuvo a punto de tirar la toalla. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-26/sanchez-y-feijoo-entran-en-modo-electoral.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

Nada que ver con el día anterior, cuando el alcalde, Javier Úbeda, reconoce que pasaron un mal rato hasta que el viento cambió de dirección. El fuego del <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/incendios-forestales/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/incendios-forestales/">gran incendio </a>que arrasa el suroeste de la Comunidad de Madrid ha afectado a pequeños pueblos de la zona rural, la más periférica de la región. De haber penetrado hacia la capital, las llamas hubieran afectado a los municipios acomodados y mucho más poblados como Villanueva de la Cañada, Villaviciosa de Odón o Boadilla, donde se asientan lo que algunos llaman urbanizaciones bosque, entornos privilegiados pero expuestos al peligro de los incendios.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-07-26/la-espana-rica-de-las-urbanizaciones-bosque-siente-cerca-el-peligro-del-fuego-en-algun-momento-nos-puede-pasar.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/BFUDUHNLI5BORMAB42EK44GV6I.jpeg?auth=5aa00880c11f0960753601bf1a2992cb6a0fdd23a4cf75b8f2415c6cfc15b3e0" width="2000" height="1500" alt="Varios comensales sentados este sábado a primera hora de la tarde en la terraza de Le Port, un restaurante con vistas al monte de Boadilla."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/FSRP5IBXK5GRZDQBFUWMZHRM6M.jpeg?auth=e6bb7c25c26725fecf1b370cbc5165cbb581e3e1c59f6c2572308abbce3cd98e" width="2000" height="1500" alt="El alcalde de Boadilla del Monte, Javier Úbeda, reunido este sábado por la mañana con varios responsables de seguridad del municipio."></img>

articles.body: <p>El incendio que recorre Madrid a toda velocidad parece tener conciencia propia. Hace unas horas se dividía en tres frentes que ahora, tras atraerse y fundirse en un todo por la dinámica de las corrientes de aire, forman una sola lengua de fuego que arrasa allá por donde pasa. Y, como si tuviera claro a dónde apuntar, se acercó con mala intención a la base de su principal enemigo: el Puesto de Mando Avanzado (PAM) desde donde las autoridades diseñan la estrategia para combatirlo.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-07-26/cuando-evacuacion-es-la-palabra-del-dia-ninos-vecinos-sin-piernas-perros-y-tambien-autoridades.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

El relato se quiere fijar ahora en las consecuencias económicas que puede tener para España no agilizar el perdón judicial de los encausados por el <i>procés</i>. La demanda de una posible reclamación compensatoria aflora tras haber denunciado ante la Comisión Europea las trabas que pone <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-21/la-fiscalia-reclama-al-tribunal-de-cuentas-que-aplique-la-amnistia-tras-el-aval-de-la-justicia-europea.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-21/la-fiscalia-reclama-al-tribunal-de-cuentas-que-aplique-la-amnistia-tras-el-aval-de-la-justicia-europea.html">el Tribunal de Cuentas al carpetazo</a> de la causa relacionada con la procedencia del dinero que se gastó para financiar el desafío independentista y el intento de referéndum de 2017. En ese escrito de denuncia presentado en Bruselas, Gonzalo Boye, que también actúa en representación de los exconsejeros Toni Comín y Lluís Puig, ya <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-17/la-aplicacion-plena-de-la-amnistia-queda-en-manos-del-constitucional-y-el-supremo-tras-el-aval-del-tjue.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-17/la-aplicacion-plena-de-la-amnistia-queda-en-manos-del-constitucional-y-el-supremo-tras-el-aval-del-tjue.html">advierte al Tribunal Supremo</a> de que tendrá que hacer frente a una indemnización por daños y perjuicios si persevera en demorar la amnistía a los políticos independentistas. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-07-25/el-caso-del-profesor-austriaco-que-esgrime-carles-puigdemont-para-pedir-una-indemnizacion-a-espana.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/5DUDX7MNJBEFZHOD26PBL7NSNE.jpg?auth=e9f698fec3ca40342bdd740e2eb2ae84e4396131e2be371f4bfd427ed249647d" width="5476" height="3981" alt="En la imagen Gonzalo Boye, abogado de Carles Puigdemont, en su despacho del paseo de Gràcia de Barcelona."></img>

articles.body: El Barça ja sap que formarà part del bombo 1 en el sorteig de la fase de lliga de la Champions League 2026-27 , una condició que li garanteix evitar alguns dels grans favorits europeus en aquesta primera fase. Tot i això, els blaugrana s’enfrontaran igualment a dos rivals del seu mateix pot , ja que el nou format de la competició preveu vuit partits contra equips de quatre bombos diferents, amb quatre duels a casa i quatre a domicili. També et pot interessar Adeyemi té clar amb qui pot entendre’s al Barça: “La connexió amb Lamine Yamal pot ser molt bona” Marina Garrido 1 minut de lectura Sis equips de talla mundial que poden ser rivals dels blaugrana Entre els possibles adversaris del Barça hi ha sis equips de primeríssim nivell: el Bayern de Múnic , el París Saint-Germain , el Manchester City , l’ Inter de Milà , l’ Arsenal i el Liverpool . Qui també forma part del bombo, però no pot encreuar-se amb els blaugrana a la fase de lliga per ser equips espanyols són el Reial Madrid i l’ Atlètic de Madrid . El sorteig, previst per al 27 d’agost, definirà el camí dels de Hansi Flick en una Champions que manté el mateix format estrenat la temporada passada i que tornarà a reunir 36 equips en una única fase de lliga.

Es manté el respir matinal, però la calor intensa ja torna a ser a la cantonada. Matinada i matí de dilluns amb mínimes entre els 22 i 24 ºC . El comptador de nits tòrrides podria seguir aturat al centre de la ciutat. Ara bé, podria tornar a engegar motors a mitjans de setmana amb l’arribada d’un altre episodi de calor més intensa . Caldrà, doncs, aprofitar aquest respir com si es tractés d’un regal , aquesta pausa perquè serà difícil trobar-la a mesura que avancin els dies. Màximes aquest dilluns al voltant dels 30 ºC. És per això que, com a consell, faríeu bé de no deixar roba estesa a l’exterior. Més enllà dels núvols i ruixats matinals esperem una jornada plàcida i estiuenca. Domini del sol, a estones enterbolit per l’arribada dels fums dels incendis de l’interior peninsular i de França. articles.body: Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FGC) inicia el dilluns 27 de juliol les tasques de revisió anual del funicular de Vallvidrera . Aquests treballs duraran un mes, fins al divendres 28 d’agost. Durant aquest període, Ferrocarrils garantirà la mobilitat de les persones usuàries i habilitarà un servei alternatiu per carretera, amb autobusos, amb el mateix horari que el servei habitual del funicular. Aquest mitjà de transport l’utilitzen diàriament unes 4.000 persones. Manteniment preventiu anual En aquestes setmanes, l’empresa dels FGC durà a terme com cada any els treballs de manteniment preventiu anual que s’han de realitzar a les instal·lacions de transport per cable, com és el cas d’un funicular. Entre aquests treballs destaca la revisió dels components mecànics i de control de la sala de màquines, del traçat i dels dos vehicles. Enguany, a més de les tasques pròpies de la revisió anual, es realitzarà la revisió general dels dos vehicles del funicular de Vallvidrera que es fa cada 10 anys als tallers dels FGC. També et pot interessar Talls al metro de Barcelona a l’estiu: L1, L9/L10, Verdaguer i l’enllaç de Catalunya | MAPA Eva Vial 2 minuts de lectura Servei alternatiu per carretera Durant el mes que el funicular estigui fora de servei, Ferrocarrils habilitarà un servei alternatiu per carretera amb el mateix horari que el servei habitual. Els autobusos pararan a les tres estacions del traçat del funicular: Peu del Funicular, Carretera de les Aigües i Vallvidrera Superior . Els punts de parada d’aquest servei substitutori es troben al costat de les estacions. En el cas de l’estació de Carretera de les Aigües, les persones usuàries hauran de sol·licitar aquest servei a través de l’intèrfon de l’estació. Característiques del servei La línia té una longitud de 736,6 metres amb un desnivell de 158 m i un pendent màxim del 29 % . El servei s’ofereix amb dos vehicles amb capacitat per a 50 persones cadascun. El temps de recorregut és de menys de tres minuts . Serveix de transport públic habitual per a les persones residents a Vallvidrera i els caps de setmana és habitual per a les persones que pugen a Collserola per realitzar caminades a la carretera de les Aigües o excursions entre Vallvidrera i altres punts del massís en què els FGC disposen també d’estacions que permeten fer el retorn en tren. També et pot interessar Passejada dels veïns dels barris de muntanya per demanar la reobertura dels camins de Collserola Andrea Muñoz 2 minuts de lectura Un funicular amb més de 100 anys d’història El funicular de Vallvidrera, construït per la companyia del Ferrocarril Sarrià Barcelona (FSB), es va inaugurar l’octubre del 1906 per tal de poder comunicar la línia del Vallès (estació de Peu del Funicular) amb el poble de Vallvidrera. El 1979 es va integrar a la xarxa de Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya. Després de diverses reformes dels cotxes antics, el 1998 els FGC va procedir a realitzar una reforma integral de la línia: es va canviar tota la plataforma de via, les estacions i els vehicles, que permeten que el funicular funcioni de manera totalment automàtica, amb la via protegida amb portes d’andana a les estacions. funicular vallvidrera També et pot interessar Negocis de Vallvidrera agonitzen amb les restriccions per la pesta porcina: “Haurem de tancar” Montse Llorens 3 minuts de lectura

articles.body: (ACN) L’ Institut Català de Finances (ICF) ha ofert a les empreses de lleure i autònoms afectats per la reducció de la seva activitat una línia de préstecs bonificats d’entre 25.000 i 100.000 euros . L’ICF vol ajudar així un sector que ha vist com la demanda de reserves de cases de colònies ha caigut per la protesta dels docents sobre les sortides escolars el curs que ve. Tot i això, les associacions ACELLEC i ACCAC consideren “insuficient” aquesta ajuda, perquè comporta demanar un crèdit, i no tenen assegurades més ajudes. A més, han reclamat al Departament d’Empresa que activi ajudes imminents per pal·liar la “crisi” : “La situació és extremament complexa. Som espectadors de pedra”, han lamentat les associacions del lleure a l’ACN. També et pot interessar Les cases de colònies reclamen al govern ajudes “el més aviat possible” Redacció 1 minut de lectura Regularitzar les sortides, la solució pel sector Des de l’Associació d’Empreses de Lleure, l’Educació i la Cultura (ACELLEC) i l’Associació de cases de colònies (ACCAC) van insistir dilluns en una reunió amb Empresa i Educació que cal regularitzar les sortides escolars de manera “formal” per integrar-les al sistema educatiu. I van defensar que aquesta és la via per assegurar el futur del sector i, alhora, atendre les demandes dels docents que participen de les mateixes colònies. Les dues associacions van manifestar que és la demanda “més important i prioritària” del sector del lleure. Però van constatar que el govern no té “cap voluntat decidida” per afrontar aquesta petició: “No ens van donar cap seguretat”, tal com han relatat des de les entitats. També et pot interessar Les cases de colònies, sense reserves per al curs vinent: “Estem a zero” Núria Granados 3 minuts de lectura Demanen ajudes imminents Pel que fa als préstecs bonificats de fins a 100.000 euros, les entitats opinen que “ és poc i insuficient . Però de moment és el que ens han donat”. És en aquest sentit l’ACELLEC i l’ACCAC van insistir que necessiten ajudes econòmiques imminents . Segons expliquen les dues associacions del lleure, el govern només els va dir que al setembre “començarien a estudiar les condicions dels possibles ajuts”. Les entitats asseguren que la situació és “extremament complexa” i que ja hi ha empreses del lleure que estudien aplicar un ERTO als seus treballadors . Una mesura que les entitats del sector assumeixen que és “més que probable” que tingui lloc. “Sí, pot ser una realitat si el govern no ens ajuda”, han asseverat les fonts consultades.

articles.body: Aquest dijous, 23 de juliol, la temperatura de l’aigua del mar a Barcelona, en concret a l’espigó del Gas a la platja de la Barceloneta , va assolir els 28,4 ºC. Una xifra que es col·loca directament al podi de les més elevades . Exactament correspon a la segona temperatura més alta anotada a la sèrie d’en Diego Lázaro, el meteoròleg i observador que en fa el seguiment des del 2006. També et pot interessar L’aigua del mar a la Barceloneta registra 26,5 ºC a finals de juny: el valor més alt des del 2006 Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 2 minuts de lectura A una dècima del rècord i abans de refredar-se A les 13.25 h (TU) d’aquest dijous, 23 de juliol, la temperatura de l’aigua del mar va arribar als 28,4 ºC a un metre de fondària davant de la platja de la Barceloneta . Es tracta del segon registre més alt de la sèrie de mesures que Diego Lázaro recull setmanalment des de fa vint anys , només superat pels 28,5 ºC observats el 21 de juliol del 2022 i el 24 d’agost del 2023. Tot plegat s’emmarca en un context de calor marina excepcional a la Mediterrània, amb temperatures molt per sobre de l’habitual. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) Els quaderns d’estiu ja no són només cosa de nens. Les propostes per a adults s’han convertit en un dels fenòmens editorials de la temporada. “És el punt mitjà entre un reel d’Instagram i una novel·la”, defensa Josep Maria Bunyol, guionista, mentre Xavi Noriguis atribueix l’èxit a una “petita desconnexió digital”. Noriguis creu que “la gent a l’estiu té ganes de fer una minidesconnexió digital “. A més, hi afegeix un altre ingredient: “És un quadern d’adults, i el pot agafar des d’una persona de 20 anys, fins a una altra de 80″ . Alguns compradors declaren que ja és una rutina anual anar a comprar “el quadern de vacances”. I cada cop hi ha més adeptes. Per exemple, una veïna del Clot s’ha sumat a la moda recentment: “Justament aquest estiu tinc l’interès de comprar llibres de passatemps”, i admet que està especialment “enganxada als sudoku”. També et pot interessar La llibreria Casa Anita rep el Premi Boixareu Ginesta al llibreter de l’any Manel Carrasco 2 minuts de lectura Més oferta en català L’èxit comercial ha animat moltes editorials a ampliar l’oferta en català, cada cop amb una presència més habitual als rànquings de vendes. La tendència la va impulsar Blackie Books , que fa més de quinze anys que publica el Quadern Blackie i acumula més de mig milió d’exemplars venuts arreu del món. En fa tres que també està disponible en català, amb 50.000 llibrets venuts . Altres editorials també s’hi han sumat, com Columna o Penguin . “Gaudir del coneixement” Altres creadors coincideixen a dir que la clau de l’èxit no és només el format, sinó la manera com s’entén el coneixement. “Reivindiquem gaudir del coneixement , passar-t’ho bé sense cap més intenció que divertir-te”, explica Maria Junyent, que apunta que “la gent té ganes de fer coses per plaer de fer-les, sense que impliquin un mòbil”. També et pot interessar Ferran Garcia i Marina Garcés, guardonats amb el XXVII Premi Llibreter Mercè Alsina 3 minuts de lectura Quaderns de nínxol De la mateixa manera ho veu Josep Maria Bunyol, juntament amb l’il·lustrador GuiBo ha publicat enguany la primera edició del Quadern de passatemps històrics . El seu volum també ha entrat als rànquings en sis de les set setmanes que està a les llibreries, i és mou entre la cinquena i la desena posició. L’èxit de vendes ha animat altres editorials a incorporar propostes similars als seus catàlegs, sovint apostant per temàtiques cada vegada més especialitzades. És el cas d’ Ara Llibres , que ha apostat per diverses edicions del Paraulògic en format físic. Els més demandats, esgotats A les llibreries han notat la demanda per aquest mercat en creixement. Maite Sánchez, propietària de la llibreria Pebre Negre, assegura que s’ha disparat “des de fa un parell d’anys”. El més buscat és el Quadern Blackie: “No el tenim perquè s’està esgotant tota l’estona” , ha declarat. La llibretera també destaca que “ara n’hi ha molts de misteris i enigmes que van més enllà dels sudoku”, com els Murdoku, un altres dels quaderns més buscats.

articles.body: (ACN) Les persones afectades per un accident de trànsit i els seus representants ja poden demanar telemàticament l’informe pericial extrajudicial a l’Institut de Medicina Legal i Ciències Forenses. Per a fer-ho, s’ha posat en marxa un canal específic a través del portal de Tràmits de la Generalitat. Aquest informe permet disposar d’una valoració medicoforense especialitzada sobre lesions i seqüeles patides per, d’aquesta manera, facilitar la resolució de conflictes entre afectats i companyies asseguradores sense necessitat d’arribar als tribunals. Nous avantatges i menys espera Abans moltes sol·licituds es presentaven a través de peticions genèriques o correu electrònic. A partir d’ara, però, hi ha un únic canal telemàtic per presentar la documentació. A més, les sol·licituds presentades s’incorporen automàticament al sistema de gestió de l’Institut de Medicina Legal. Això en facilita el seguiment, permet una distribució més eficient entre els diversos territoris, agilitza la tramitació i redueix els errors administratius. Segons ha informat el Departament de Justícia, la normativa estableix que els representants de les víctimes, principalment despatxos d’advocats i altres professionals, estan obligats a relacionar-se electrònicament amb l’Administració. Per això, a partir d’ara, les sol·licituds que s’enviïn per altres canals no seran admeses. En canvi, la normativa preveu una excepció per a les persones físiques que no estan obligades a relacionar-se electrònicament amb l’Administració.

articles.body: (ACN) La temperatura fa un mes que no baixa dels 24 °C al centre de Barcelona, on prop de 2.000 persones dormen al carrer. La calor extrema afecta tothom, però l’impacte és més gran per a qui no té un sostre on refugiar-se. Les altes temperatures també colpegen el sensellarisme : el 58 % de la gent en situació de carrer no pot descansar, segons Arrels . També et pot interessar Arrels demana a l’Ajuntament més facilitats perquè els sensesostre es puguin refugiar de la calor Redacció 3 minuts de lectura Els estius, cada vegada “més difícils” En Dani ha dormit al ras fa més de vuit anys, i ha explicat a l’ACN que “molta gent que viu al carrer mor per la calor”. Des del taller d’Arrels, remarca que “no tothom té la sort” de tenir “una casa on dutxar-se”. Relata que les administracions recomanen que, durant l’estiu, tothom s’hidrati i es refresqui sovint, eviti les hores punta de més calor, i busqui ombres: “Tot això si tens la sort de tenir una casa”, ha matisat. Dormir al carrer durant l’estiu és molt difícil, assegura en Dani, que reitera que cada vegada és més complicat “sobreviure” a les temperatures extremes: “Aquest any fa molta calor, i sense aigua corrent és difícil per a tothom”. “Ara la gent que viu al carrer té molta calor, i molta gent mor per la calor . És difícil buscar ombres”, afirma. També et pot interessar El 72 % de les persones que viuen al carrer no tenen expectatives de deixar de viure al ras Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura Prohibició d’ús de les dutxes Així mateix, lamenta que abans, a la nit, podien anar a les dutxes de les platges , però que ara ja no ho poden fer, d’acord amb les ordenances municipals . A més, a moltes persones en situació de sensellarisme les desperten la policia o les brigades de neteja: “Abans els agents no molestaven mai quan dormies. Ara hi ha més vigilància, aquest any és pitjor”, ha asseverat. També et pot interessar Barcelona estrena la nova ordenança de civisme, amb més multes i prohibicions Marta de San Nicolás 2 minuts de lectura Ocupació dels espais La directora d’Arrels reitera, en una entrevista a l’ACN, que l’estiu afecta “negativament” les persones que viuen al carrer. Fernández detalla que la calor afecta la salut física, sobretot a qui tingui problemes crònics i cardiovasculars. Les altes temperatures també provoquen molts problemes per descansar. Durant l’estiu, la població aprofita per ser més al carrer i s’ocupen més els espais públics, tal com explica Fernández: “Els horaris s’allarguen i la gent fa més vida fora de casa fins a la nit”. Que la gent faci més activitat als carrers durant la nit també fa que calgui més manteniment, i les brigades de neteja actuen més sovint i més d’hora. Aquest fet també impacta en les persones que intenten dormir al ras. “Tot això incrementa l’estrès que ja suposa viure al carrer”, reflexiona la directora d’Arrels. Manca de refugis climàtics Fernández també comenta que no tots els refugis climàtics de Barcelona estan disponibles per a la gent amb situació de carrer durant l’estiu. Per exemple, algunes biblioteques municipals tanquen, o bé no s’hi pot accedir amb les pertinences d’aquestes persones. També et pot interessar Refugis climàtics a Barcelona 2026: Tots els punts on combatre la calor aquest estiu | MAPA Eva Vial 2 minuts de lectura D’altres espais també abaixen la persiana perquè els professionals o voluntaris fan vacances. Per això les persones amb situació de carrer veuen reduïdes les opcions on rentar-se i refrescar-se, i es veuen abocades a utilitzar fonts públiques. Però les ordenances de Barcelona en prohibeixen l’ús per a aquesta utilitat. És per això que Arrels reclama que la policia “no sancioni” qui utilitzi les fonts per la seva situació de sensellarisme. “Calen espais de molta baixa exigència, més espais d’emergència i allotjaments nocturns”, explica Fernández. Així mateix, la directora de la fundació insta les administracions a mirar “més enllà” de l’estiu, per entendre que el canvi climàtic “impacta directament” en la vida de la gent que dorm al ras. És per això que les apressa a aplicar “solucions més transversals i de llarga durada”, amb allotjament “estables i perdurables”.
